questions.question: Why does a hot-air balloon rise, and what was the main problem with balloons for transport?
questions.expected_answer: A hot-air balloon rises because the hot air inside it is lighter than the cooler air around it. The main problem is that balloons cannot be steered; they go wherever the wind blows.

questions.question: What is an airship, and why did people stop using airships for passengers?
questions.expected_answer: An airship is a long balloon filled with a gas lighter than air, with engines and propellers so it can be steered. People stopped using them for passengers after the Hindenburg, filled with hydrogen, caught fire in 1937 and thirty-six people died.

questions.question: Name two kinds of modern air transport and explain how each one helps people.
questions.expected_answer: Jet aeroplanes carry hundreds of passengers and goods such as post, medicine and fresh fruit quickly over long distances. Helicopters can take off straight up, hover and land in small spaces, so they rescue people, fight fires and carry patients to hospital as air ambulances.
